title: Unicon grading plan
description: What the backend's compiler emits when a task is published: a flat list of primitive calls with every workflow reference already resolved, pinned to one grading image by digest. The harness executes a plan; it never reads workflow YAML.

schema_version.description: The plan shape this file is written against. The harness refuses a version it does not speak, because a compiler that emits a shape the harness reads differently produces a wrong verdict rather than an error.

image_digest.description: The grading image this plan was compiled against, by content digest and never by tag, so a task keeps grading on the image it was published with.

stage.description: The grading stage this plan belongs to. A task may compile a different plan per stage.

steps.description: Run in order. Each step may read the outputs of earlier steps.

id.description: Unique within the plan. Earlier steps are referred to by this id.

primitive.description: Which tool in the grading image to call, as owner/name@version, for example unicon/sandbox-run@v1. Must be a primitive listed in the registry.json of the pinned runner release; composed workflows are already inlined by the compiler.

inputs.description: Arguments for the primitive, keyed by the input names in the registry. Deliberately open: the value grammar for naming bundle paths and earlier step outputs is settled by the compiler and the primitives in Task 10.

for_each.description: Run this step once per item of the named list and collect the outputs into an array. The reference grammar is the compiler's; the harness only needs it to name a list it can already see.

limits.description: Sandbox limits for one run of this step. Open on purpose: Task 6 decides what else the sandbox enforces.

time_ms.description: Wall clock for one run. The sandbox is killed when it passes.

cpu_ms.description: CPU time for one run, the innermost of the three timers in TASK-FORMAT.md. Usually below time_ms.

memory_mb.description: Memory cap for the sandbox. Over-limit is a kill, not a slowdown.

pids.description: Process limit, what stops a fork bomb.

output_mb.description: How much the step may write before it is cut off.
